title: Admired musicians: violinist Everett Lee
summary: He praises Everett Lee, who conducted for Carmen Jones, and has tried to get him a Grant Park date.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Can you tell me some of your favorite musicians that you've heard? I'm not trying to put you on the spot, because I know that you're in your... Well, there's so many. There's so many. I have... I mean some of the old timers maybe that aren't even living now on different instruments that you've liked.

Well, there are a lot of... Among the newcomers that I admire greatly and have all the respect in the world for them on various instruments. There's a young fella I met about four or five years ago. He's originally from Cleveland. He's living in New York now. Violinist by the name of Everett Lee. He's also a very fine composer. He has toured Europe. The last card I had from, he was touring South America, conducting all the various symphonies there. When he first came to New York, it was just when Carmen Jones had started. Leonard Bernstein had the orchestra.

Leonard Bernstein was so carried away with his talent that they made him the concert master of that orchestra. And any time Leonard felt that he wanted to take a rest, he let Everett take the orchestra. And after they closed the season in New York and went on the road, he didn't leave New York. He sent Everett Lee with the outfit.

Since I met him and heard him and saw him in action, I've been trying to get him a date here in Chicago to Grant Park. I haven't been successful so far. They always have some lame excuse. But the boy has done a grand, grand job.
